import { Aside } from '@astrojs/starlight/components';
import SeqDiagram from '../../../../components/SeqDiagram.astro';

**Task:** accept private documents from your app's members, process them
without any code but a compute run ever reading them, and run the same
multi-step job (one step per document, then one that joins the results) on
hundreds of files at a time.

Three pieces, each built on the one before:

1. **Sealed files**: a member uploads a file, the app keeps a `BlobRef` to it,
   and only a compute run can read its bytes.
2. **Compute runs**: a method marked `#[app::compute]` runs on a job node over
   files and writes new files.
   How to write, build, start and test one is in
   [Compute actions](/build/guides/compute-actions/); this guide uses it.
3. **Pipelines**: a YAML file shipped in the release names compute steps and
   how they connect; the node runs it as compute runs, without a call per step.

The example is a word counter.
The Rust code builds for both components, and the pipeline passes
`calimero_pipeline::compile` and `check` against the app's compute methods.

## Files or blobs

| | Plain blob | Sealed file |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Uploaded with | `POST /apps/{app}/blobs` (`meroctl blob upload`) | `POST /apps/{app}/files`, or an upload session for a large one (`meroctl file upload`) |
| Who may upload | a signed-in account the app's access admits | the app's owner and its organization's members |
| Size | 47 MiB | 2 GiB per file, uploaded in 16 MiB parts |
| App code reads the bytes | no (`BlobRef::info` only) | only inside a compute run (`files::open`) |
| Leaves the cluster | `GET .../blobs/{id}` with a session or a grant | only through an export, sealed to the requester's key, or as a published compute output |

For blobs, and `grant` links, see [Files and blobs](/build/guides/blobs/).
The rest of this page is about sealed files.

## Keep a member's file

The member uploads first, then calls a method with the file's id, which a
`BlobRef` parameter takes as a 64-hex string:

```bash
meroctl file upload ./report.txt -c docs        # prints { id, size, sha256, index }
meroctl call -c docs submit --args '{"file":"<id>"}'
```

```ts
const { id } = await client.uploadFile(app, fileFromInput);   // mero-js: one request, or parts that resume
await client.apps.call({ app, method: 'submit', args: { file: id } });
```

```rust
use calimero_sdk::blob::BlobRef;
use calimero_sdk::compute::{self, ComputeOutcome, ComputeStatus, RunId};
use calimero_sdk::files;
use calimero_sdk::prelude::*;

#[app::state(version = 1)]
pub struct DocIndex {
    /// The documents submitted, by file id: a reference in state keeps the file.
    docs: UnorderedMap<String, BlobRef>,
    /// The count files runs made, by file id.
    counts: UnorderedMap<String, BlobRef>,
}

#[app::error]
pub enum Error {
    NoSuchFile,
    NotYourFile,
}

/// A document as `doc` describes it (D20: the size as a decimal string).
#[derive(serde::Serialize)]
pub struct DocOut {
    pub size: String,
    pub uploader: Option<String>,
}

/// `countWords`'s arguments.
#[derive(serde::Serialize)]
#[serde(rename_all = "camelCase")]
struct CountArgs {
    min_len: u32,
}

#[app::logic]
impl DocIndex {
    #[app::init]
    pub fn init() -> app::Result<Self> {
        Ok(Self::load())
    }

    /// Keep a file the caller uploaded, and count its words in a compute run.
    pub fn submit(&mut self, file: BlobRef) -> app::Result<RunId> {
        let Some(_info) = files::info(&file) else {
            app::bail!(Error::NoSuchFile);
        };
        let me = guards::require_member()?;
        if files::uploader(&file).as_deref() != Some(me.as_str()) {
            app::bail!(Error::NotYourFile);
        }
        self.docs.insert(&file.id(), &file)?;
        compute::start("countWords", &CountArgs { min_len: 1 }, &[file])
    }

    /// A kept document's size and uploader; its bytes stay sealed.
    #[app::view]
    pub fn doc(&self, file: BlobRef) -> app::Result<Option<DocOut>> {
        if self.docs.get(&file.id())?.is_none() {
            return Ok(None);
        }
        Ok(files::info(&file).map(|info| DocOut {
            size: info.size.to_string(),
            uploader: files::uploader(&file),
        }))
    }

    // countWords, join and onCounted: below.
}
```

- `files::info(&file)` is `Some(FileInfo { size, sha256 })` for a sealed file
  the app holds, else `None`. It works in every kind of run but a migration.
- `files::uploader(&file)` is the account the node recorded from the
  authenticated upload: `None` for a file a call or a run made, and not
  available inside a compute run.
  It is how an app decides who may submit what.
- **A reference in state is what keeps a file.**
  An uploaded file nothing refers to is forgotten an hour later
  (`BLOB_IDLE_MS`), and so is one whose last `BlobRef` the app removes.
  There is no delete call: drop the reference.
- Outside a compute run `files::open` traps (`HostDenied`: "a sealed file is
  readable only inside a compute run"), so no call or view can leak the bytes
  into state, an event or a result.

A call, timer or `init` may also write a file with `files::create()` (a
`std::io::Write`; `finish()` answers the `BlobRef`), at most 64 MiB per run.

## Process it in a compute run

```rust
use std::io::{BufRead, BufReader, Write};

    /// Writes one line per input, `<file id> <words>`, counting words of at least `min_len`
    /// characters. Runs on a job node.
    #[app::compute(fuel = 50_000_000_000, memory_mib = 128, wall_secs = 120, result = "on_counted")]
    pub fn count_words(min_len: u32) -> app::Result<u64> {
        let mut out = files::create()?;
        let mut total = 0u64;
        let inputs = compute::inputs();
        for (i, input) in inputs.iter().enumerate() {
            let mut words = 0u64;
            for line in BufReader::new(files::open(input)?).lines() {
                let line = line?;
                let long = line
                    .split_whitespace()
                    .filter(|w| w.chars().count() >= min_len as usize);
                words += long.count() as u64;
            }
            compute::progress((100 * (i + 1) / inputs.len()) as u8, "counting");
            writeln!(out, "{} {words}", input.id())?;
            total += words;
        }
        out.finish()?;
        Ok(total)
    }

    /// Joins every input into one file, in the order given.
    #[app::compute(fuel = 50_000_000_000, memory_mib = 128, wall_secs = 120, result = "on_counted")]
    pub fn join() -> app::Result<u32> {
        let mut out = files::create()?;
        let inputs = compute::inputs();
        for input in &inputs {
            std::io::copy(&mut files::open(input)?, &mut out)?;
        }
        out.finish()?;
        Ok(inputs.len() as u32)
    }

    /// The node runs this when a run the app started ends; it keeps the outputs.
    #[app::compute_result]
    pub fn on_counted(&mut self, outcome: ComputeOutcome) -> app::Result<()> {
        if outcome.status == ComputeStatus::Done {
            for output in &outcome.outputs {
                self.counts.insert(&output.id.id(), &output.id)?;
            }
        }
        Ok(())
    }
```

`submit` starts `countWords` over one file, and `on_counted` stores the output's
`BlobRef`, which is what keeps it.
The rules (caps, determinism, result methods, publishing an output, the
`mero-app-build --compute-out` build and the `mero-compute` test runner) are in
[Compute actions](/build/guides/compute-actions/).
In a compute run, files are bounded by `MAX_FILE_BYTES` (2 GiB each) and 2 GiB
written in all, 16 open at once, and 1,000 new files.

## Ship a pipeline

Starting one run per file from a call works for a few files.
For hundreds, with a step that waits for all of them, ship a pipeline: the
leader decides each step from the run's record and starts its compute runs in
waves, and a client starts the whole thing with one request.

`pipelines/wordcount.yaml`:

```yaml
apiVersion: compute.calimero.network/v1
kind: Pipeline
name: wordcount
params:
  min-len: { type: number, default: 1, min: 1, max: 64 }
inputs:
  docs: { kind: files, maxItems: 500 }
steps:
  count:
    method: countWords
    forEach: inputs.docs
    maxItems: 500
    batch: 10
    maxParallel: 8
    allowFailures: 5%
    args: { minLen: params.min-len }
    limits: { wallSecs: 60 }
  total:
    method: join
    collect: count.outputs
outputs: [total.outputs]
```

| Field | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `apiVersion`, `kind`, `name` | Required: `compute.calimero.network/v1`, `Pipeline`, and a name of 1 to 64 characters of `[a-z0-9-]` starting with a letter (the same rule for every step, input and param name; `inputs`, `params` and `item` are reserved). |
| `module` | The module steps run in when they name none: `self` (the release's own compute component, the default) or another installed package, `com.acme.pdf[@0.1.0]`, pinned at install. |
| `params` | Typed values a run passes: `type` (`number`, `string`, `boolean`), `default`, `min`, `max`, `enum`. A step reads one as `params.<name>`. |
| `inputs` | What a run binds: `kind: files` (with `maxItems`), `artifact` or `table` (one file each), and an optional `default`. |
| `steps.<name>.method` | A compute method of the step's module, by its ABI name (`countWords`). |
| `args` | The method's arguments, a JSON object whose values may be `params.x`, `<step>.result` or, in a fan-out, `item`. A method that takes none gets none. |
| `inputs` (step) | Files the run gets: `inputs.x`, `<step>.outputs`, and `item` in a fan-out. |
| `needs` | Steps that must succeed first; a reference to a step adds it. |
| `forEach` | One item per file of `inputs.x` or `<step>.outputs`, or per value of `<step>.results`; needs `maxItems`. `batch` groups items into one run, `maxParallel` bounds the runs active at once, `allowFailures` (a count or a percentage) lets the step succeed with some items failed. |
| `collect` | `<fan-out step>.outputs`: one run over all of that step's outputs, in item order. |
| `limits` | `fuel`, `memoryMib`, `wallSecs`: only lower than the method's caps. |
| `pool` | Run this step's runs on that pool's job nodes. |
| `cache` | `false` turns the step cache off for this step (default on). |
| `outputs`, `failFast` | The run's outputs; `failFast: true` cancels the other steps at the first failed one. |

`when`, `runIf`, `uses`, `loops`, `variables`, `sources`, `sinks`, `publish`,
`notify` and an input's `accept`, `maxFileSize`, `format` and `schema` are
refused with `NOT_IN_V1`, never ignored.
A source is at most 64 KiB, with at most 64 steps, 64 inputs, 64 params and
10,000 items per fan-out (`crates/pipeline/src/compile.rs`).

### Check it before you pack

```bash
meroctl pipeline validate pipelines/wordcount.yaml                          # structure only
meroctl pipeline validate pipelines/wordcount.yaml --package com.example.docs --version 1.0.0
```

`POST /pipelines/validate` lists every problem with its `path` and stable
`code` (`BAD_NAME`, `BAD_REF`, `CYCLE`, `NOT_IN_V1`, `MISSING_MODULE`, ...) and
writes nothing; against an installed release it also checks the methods and
caps the release would give it, and answers `worstCaseFuel` (and
`worstCaseCost` when the operator has set prices).

### Pack it into the release

```bash
mero-app-build apps/doc-index --out app.wasm --compute-out compute.wasm
python3 -I scripts/pack-component.py --wasm app.wasm --compute compute.wasm \
  --pipeline pipelines/wordcount.yaml \
  --package com.example.docs --app-version 1.0.0 --key my-signing-key.json \
  --out dist/com.example.docs-1.0.0.mpk
```

The manifest lists the file under `pipelines` (at most 16 per package, each at
most 64 KiB), signed with the rest.
At install the node compiles each one and checks it against the release's
compute methods, the modules it names and the cluster's pools.
Any problem refuses the release with `400 BAD_PIPELINE` and `details: [{ file,
path, code, message }]` for every error (`NO_COMPUTE` for a release without a
compute component, `DUPLICATE_NAME` for two pipelines of one name); a
multi-service package declaring pipelines is `422 PIPELINES_NEED_ONE_SERVICE`.
A release with pipelines installs only once every node runs this release
(`409 CLUSTER_NOT_UPGRADED`).
`meroctl app pipelines com.example.docs` prints what a version registered:
each pipeline's hash, worst-case fuel, pinned modules and canonical JSON.

## Run it

<SeqDiagram id="d-guide-pipeline" title="One pipeline run: a fan-out over three files, then a collect"
  lanes={[
    { label: 'Client', color: '#f0883e' },
    { label: 'App leader', color: '#58a6ff' },
    { label: 'App log', color: '#a371f7' },
    { label: 'Job nodes', color: '#39d0d8' },
  ]}
  steps={[
    { from: 0, to: 1, label: 'POST /apps/{app}/pipelines/wordcount/runs { inputs, params }' },
    { from: 1, to: 2, label: 'pipelineStart: inputs pinned, release and pipeline hash fixed' },
    { from: 1, to: 0, label: '202 { run }', dashed: true },
    { from: 1, to: 2, label: 'pipelineStep count: start runs .count.0 ... (a wave)' },
    { from: 1, to: 3, label: 'compute runs countWords, one per batch' },
    { from: 3, to: 1, label: 'signed reports and outputs', dashed: true },
    { from: 1, to: 2, label: 'computeFinal per run: count succeeded' },
    { from: 1, to: 2, label: 'pipelineStep total: start one run over count.outputs' },
    { from: 1, to: 3, label: 'compute run join' },
    { from: 3, to: 1, label: 'report and output', dashed: true },
    { from: 1, to: 2, label: 'computeFinal: run succeeded' },
  ]} />

```bash
meroctl file upload ./a.txt -c docs                    # one id per file
meroctl pipeline estimate docs wordcount --input docs=<id1>,<id2>,<id3>
meroctl pipeline run docs wordcount --input docs=<id1>,<id2>,<id3> \
  --param min-len=4 --max-cost 5000000 --wait
meroctl pipeline watch docs <run>                      # snapshot, run and step events, then end
meroctl pipeline receipt docs <run> --verify
meroctl pipeline download docs <run> --out ./counts    # every output as STEP-INDEX.bin
```

From mero-js the routes are generated methods of `client.apps`:

```ts
const estimate = await client.apps.pipelinesEstimateRun({ app, name: 'wordcount', counts: { docs: 120 } });
const { run } = await client.apps.pipelinesStart({
  app, name: 'wordcount', inputs: { docs: ids }, params: { 'min-len': 4 }, maxCost: '5000000',
});
const state = await client.apps.pipelinesGet({ app, run });   // each step's status, runs and reason
const bytes = await client.exportFile(app, outputId);          // checked against its hashes before it answers
```

In Python, `client.apps.pipelines_start(app=..., name="wordcount", inputs={...})`
and `pipelines_estimate_run`, and in Rust `Client::start_pipeline_run`,
`estimate_pipeline`, `pipeline_run_events`, `pipeline_receipt` and
`verify_receipt`.

What happens to the run:

- It pins the release's pipeline by hash and its compute component at start,
  so upgrading the app does not change a run already going, and a retry keeps
  the original release.
- Each step's work is ordinary compute runs with ids `<run>.<step>.<index>`,
  under the app's owner, payer and file keys.
  They have **no result method**: the step keeps each run's result (at most
  64 KiB) and outputs, held by the pipeline run's record until it is dropped
  (an app keeps its last 64 finished runs).
  Download the outputs you need, or have a call keep them.
- A step run whose method, arguments and input contents match an earlier
  successful run in the app is answered from the **step cache**, at no cost.
  `meroctl pipeline retry docs <run> --limit count.fuel=80000000000` starts a
  new run where only the failed items run again.
- `maxCost` caps what the run may owe under the operator's price table: no step
  run starts that could take it past the cap, and the step that hits it fails
  with `COST_CAP`.

The step and run rules (fan-out waves, `allowFailures`, `failFast`, pools,
cache lifetime, cost) are in [Pipeline runs](/protocol/compute-actions/#pipeline-runs);
receipts, events and exports are also covered in
[Compute actions](/build/guides/compute-actions/#pipeline-run-receipts).

## Errors

| Status, code | When |
| --- | --- |
| `400 BAD_PIPELINE` | at install: a pipeline does not compile or check; `details` lists every error |
| `404 NO_SUCH_PIPELINE` | the app's release registers no pipeline of that name |
| `400 BAD_INPUTS` | an input that is not the pipeline's, unbound, past its `maxItems`, more than 1,024 files in all, or not a file id |
| `410 OUTPUT_EXPIRED` | an input (or, on a retry, an original input) is not a file the app holds |
| `400 BAD_PARAMS` | a param of the wrong type, outside `min`/`max`/`enum`, or undeclared |
| `409 NO_PRICE_TABLE`, `400 BAD_MAX_COST` | `maxCost` given and the operator set no prices, or it is not a whole number of micro-units |
| `429 TOO_MANY_PIPELINE_RUNS` | 8 runs already going in this app |
| `403 FORBIDDEN` | the caller is not the app's owner or a member of its organization (start, cancel, retry, receipt), even on a public app |
| `409 STILL_RUNNING`, `400 LIMIT_EXCEEDS_CAP`, `400 BAD_LIMITS` | a retry of a running run, or with limits above the method's caps or for a step the pipeline lacks |
| `409 RUN_NOT_ENDED` | a receipt asked for before the run ended |
| `429 TOO_MANY_EXPORTS` | more than 30 exports a minute by one account on one node |

A step that cannot be built fails with its own code in the run's record
(`TOO_MANY_ITEMS`, `TOO_MANY_INPUTS`, `RUN_TOO_LARGE`, `COST_CAP`,
`RESULTS_TOO_LARGE`, ...): [Pipeline runs](/protocol/compute-actions/#pipeline-runs).

<Aside type="caution">
  A step cache hit reuses an earlier output for equal method, arguments and
  input contents. A method whose output varies for the same inputs (it should
  not: a compute run's clock and randomness are fixed per run) needs
  `cache: false` on its step.
</Aside>
